verses.zh: 主耶和华的灵在我身上；因为耶和华用膏膏我，叫我传好信息给谦卑的人（或译：传福音给贫穷的人），差遣我医好伤心的人，报告被掳的得释放，被囚的出监牢；
verses.en: The Spirit of the Sovereign Lord is upon me,because the Lord has chosen[NOTE:1] me.[NOTE:2] He has commissioned[NOTE:3] me to encourage[NOTE:4] the poor,to help[NOTE:5] the brokenhearted,to decree the release of captivesand the freeing of prisoners,
notes: Heb “anointed,” i.e., designated to carry out an assigned task.

The speaker is not identified, but he is distinct from the Lord and from Zion’s suffering people. He possesses the divine spirit, is God’s spokesman, and is sent to release prisoners from bondage. The evidence suggests he is the Lord’s special servant, described earlier in the servant songs (see 42:1-4, 7; 49:2, 9; 50:4; see also 51:16).
Or “sent” (NAB); NCV “has appointed me.”
Or “proclaim good news to.”
Heb “to bind up [the wounds of].”

verses.zh: 报告耶和华的恩年，和我们　神报仇的日子；安慰一切悲哀的人，
verses.en: to announce the year when the Lord will show his favor,the day when our God will seek vengeance,[NOTE:1] to console all who mourn,
notes: Heb “to announce the year of the Lord’s favor, and the day of our God’s vengeance.”

verses.zh: 赐华冠与锡安悲哀的人，代替灰尘；喜乐油代替悲哀；赞美衣代替忧伤之灵；使他们称为「公义树」，是耶和华所栽的，叫他得荣耀。
verses.en: to strengthen those who mourn in Zionby giving them a turban, instead of ashes,oil symbolizing joy,[NOTE:1] instead of mourning,a garment symbolizing praise,[NOTE:2] instead of discouragement.[NOTE:3] They will be called oaks of righteousness,[NOTE:4] trees planted by the Lord to reveal his splendor.[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “oil of joy” (KJV, ASV, NIV11); NASB, NIV84, NRSV “the oil of gladness.”
Heb “garment of praise.”
Heb “a faint spirit” (so NRSV); KJV, ASV “the spirit of heaviness”; NASB “a spirit of fainting.”

Rather than referring to the character of the people, צֶדֶק (tsedeq) may carry the nuance “vindication” here, suggesting that God’s restored people are a testimony to his justice. See v. 2, which alludes to the fact that God will take vengeance against the enemies of his people. Cf. NAB “oaks of justice.”
Heb “a planting of the Lord to reveal splendor.”

verses.zh: 他们必修造已久的荒场，建立先前凄凉之处，重修历代荒凉之城。
verses.en: They will rebuild the perpetual ruinsand restore the places that were desolate;[NOTE:1] they will reestablish the ruined cities,the places that have been desolate since ancient times.
notes: Heb “and the formerly desolate places they will raise up.”

verses.zh: 那时，外人必起来牧放你们的羊群；外邦人必作你们耕种田地的，修理葡萄园的。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “Foreigners will take care of[NOTE:2] your sheep;foreigners will work in your fields and vineyards.
notes: The Lord speaks in vv. 7-8 (and possibly v. 9). It is not clear where the servant’s speech (see vv. 1-3a) ends and the Lord’s begins. Perhaps the direct address to the people signals the beginning of the Lord’s speech.
Heb “will stand [in position] and shepherd.”

verses.zh: 你们倒要称为耶和华的祭司；人必称你们为我们　神的仆役。你们必吃用列国的财物，因得他们的荣耀自夸。
verses.en: You will be called, ‘the Lord’s priests,servants of our God.’[NOTE:1] You will enjoy[NOTE:2] the wealth of nationsand boast about[NOTE:3] the riches you receive from them.[NOTE:4]
notes: The Hebrew text adds, “it will be said concerning you.”
Heb “eat” (KJV, NAB, NASB); NIV “feed on”; NLT “be fed with.”

The form in the Hebrew text probably needs to be emended to יִתְאַמְּרוּ (yitʾammeru), a Hitpael from אָמַר (ʾamar), meaning “boast about” (see HALOT 67 s.v. II אמר, HALOT 416 s.v. ימר, and BDB 56 s.v. אָמַר).
Heb “their glory” (i.e., riches).

verses.zh: 你们必得加倍的好处，代替所受的羞辱；分中所得的喜乐，必代替所受的凌辱。在境内必得加倍的产业；永远之乐必归与你们（原文是他们）。
verses.en: Instead of shame, you will get a double portion;[NOTE:1] instead of humiliation, they will rejoice over the land they receive.[NOTE:2] Yes,[NOTE:3] they will possess a double portion in their landand experience lasting joy.
notes: Heb “instead of your shame, a double portion.”
Heb “and [instead of] humiliation they will rejoice [over] their portion.” The term תַחַת (takhat, “instead of”) is understood by ellipsis (note the preceding line).
Heb “therefore” (so KJV, NASB); NIV “and so.”

verses.zh: 因为我―耶和华喜爱公平，恨恶抢夺和罪孽；我要凭诚实施行报应，并要与我的百姓立永约。
verses.en: For I, the Lord, love justiceand hate robbery and sin.I will repay them because of my faithfulness;[NOTE:1] I will make a permanent covenant with them.
notes: Heb “in faithfulness”; NASB, NRSV, NLT “faithfully.”

verses.zh: 他们的后裔必在列国中被人认识；他们的子孙在众民中也是如此。凡看见他们的必认他们是耶和华赐福的后裔。
verses.en: Their descendants will be known among the nations,their offspring among the peoples.All who see them will recognize thatthe Lord has blessed them.”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “all who see them will recognize them, that they [are] descendants [whom] the Lord has blessed.”

verses.zh: 我因耶和华大大欢喜；我的心靠　神快乐。因他以拯救为衣给我穿上，以公义为袍给我披上，好像新郎戴上华冠，又像新妇佩戴妆饰。
verses.en: I[NOTE:1] will greatly rejoice[NOTE:2] in the Lord;I will be overjoyed because of my God.[NOTE:3] For he clothes me in garments of deliverance;he puts on me a robe symbolizing vindication.[NOTE:4] I look like a bridegroom when he wears a turban as a priest would;I look like a bride when she puts on her jewelry.[NOTE:5]
notes: The speaker in vv. 10-11 is not identified, but it is likely that the personified nation (or perhaps Zion) responds here to the Lord’s promise of restoration.
The infinitive absolute appears before the finite verb for emphasis.
Heb “my being is happy in my God”; NAB “in my God is the joy of my soul.”
Heb “robe of vindication”; KJV, NASB, NIV, NRSV “robe of righteousness.”
Heb “like a bridegroom [who] acts like a priest [by wearing] a turban, and like a bride [who] wears her jewelry.” The words “I look” are supplied for stylistic reasons and clarification.

verses.zh: 田地怎样使百谷发芽，园子怎样使所种的发生，主耶和华必照样使公义和赞美在万民中发出。
verses.en: For just as the ground produces its cropsand a garden yields its produce,so the Sovereign Lord will cause deliverance[NOTE:1] to growand give his people reason to praise him in the sight of all the nations.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or perhaps, “righteousness,” but the context seems to emphasize deliverance and restoration (see v. 10 and 62:1).
Heb “and praise before all the nations.”

READING CYCLE THREE (see
"Bible Interpretation Seminar")

FOLLOWING THE ORIGINAL AUTHOR'S INTENT AT PARAGRAPH LEVEL

This is a study guide commentary, which
means that you are responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the
light we have. You, the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not
relinquish this to a commentator.

Read the chapter in one sitting. Identify the subjects (reading cycle #3). Compare
your subject divisions with the five translations above. Paragraphing is not inspired, but it is
the key to following the original author's intent, which is the heart of interpretation. Every
paragraph has one and only one subject.

CONTEXTUAL INSIGHTS

- Isaiah 60 describes the end result, while Isa. 61 describes the means of God's blessing.

- Jesus uses this passage of Himself in Luke 4:16-21; 7:18-23. This was meant to be the task of
Israel's king. Because of this, this passage must be Messianic (i.e. the Servant).

Those of us who are Christian must continue to remember that Jesus is the ultimate revelation of
God (cf. Matt. 5:17-19). His life, teachings, death, and resurrection changed everything! The OT must
now be reinterpreted through NT revelation (cf. 2 Tim. 3:15-17). Neither Jesus nor any Apostle ever
reaffirmed a national promise to Israel. By divine act Jerusalem and the temple were destroyed by
Rome (A.D. 66-70). As a consequence of this, the Jewish believers totally separated
from the synagogue and became a truly international church (cf. Matt. 28:18-20; Luke 24:46-47; Acts 1:8)!

I have come to believe that the Olivet Discourse of Jesus (i.e. Matt. 24; Mark 13; Luke 17; 21;
2 Thess. 2; and the book of Revelation) predict the Jewish war with Rome and not far future events and
persons. Please check my exegetical verse-by-verse commentary on these verses free online at
www.freebiblecommentary.org.

- The Spirit of the Lord here is obviously analogous
(i.e. foreshadowing) to the Holy Spirit in the NT Trinitarian sense.

- see SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE

- see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

- see SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

- It is obvious that this is an example of a local historical situation in the life of Israel being used to
depict future events in the time of the Messiah (i.e. typology).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TYPOLOGY

WORD AND PHRASE STUDY

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 61:1-3

1The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me,

Because the Lord has anointed me

To bring good news to the afflicted;

He has sent me to bind up the brokenhearted,

To proclaim liberty to captives

And freedom to prisoners;

2To proclaim the favorable year of the Lord

And the day of vengeance of our God;

To comfort all who mourn,

3To grant those who mourn in Zion,

Giving them a garland instead of ashes,

The oil of gladness instead of mourning,

The mantle of praise instead of a spirit of fainting.

So they will be called oaks of righteousness,

The planting of the Lord, that He may be glorified.

61:1 "The Spirit of the Lord God is upon me" Jesus used this verse for
Himself in Luke 4:18-21. He also used this verse to answer John the Baptist's question. cf. Luke 7:18-23. This
occurred visibly in Jesus' life at His baptism (cf. Isa. 11:1-2; 42:1; Matt. 3:13-17; Mark 1:9-11; Luke 3:21,22; John 1:31-34),
but the Spirit had always been with Jesus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE PERSONHOOD OF THE SPIRIT

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE TRINITY

▣ "anointed" This is the same Hebrew root from which the title "Messiah" (BDB 602) or
"the Anointed One" comes. This was a sign of God's unique blessing and equipping for a task (cf. Ps. 23:5).
In the OT prophets, priests, and kings were anointed as a symbolic act of God's unique presence and call upon their
lives. From this John Calvin derived his threefold category for describing Christ's ministry as prophet, priest,
and king (cf. Heb. 1:2-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: ANOINTING IN THE BIBLE (BDB 603)

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIAH

▣ "To bring good news to the afflicted" The Messiah's message will be one of hope and
forgiveness to the outcast, ostracized, and socially oppressed (cf. Isa. 35:5-6; note Matt. 11:5; 12:15-22;
Luke 4:18-21; 7:18-23; John 3:16).

Notice the series of INFINITIVE CONSTRUCTS in Isa. 61:1-3 that
describe the Messiah's task.

- to bring good news to the afflicted ‒ Piel, BDB 142, KB 163

- to proclaim liberty to captives ‒ Qal, BDB 894, KB 1128

- to proclaim the favorable year of the Lord ‒ same as #2

- to comfort all who mourn ‒ Piel BDB 636, KB 688

- to grant those who mourn in Zion a garland instead of ashes

- grant ‒ Qal, BDB 962, KB 1321

- give ‒ Qal BDB 678, KB 733

- another INFINITIVE CONSTRUCT but directed towards the Messiah, Himself ‒ "that
He may be glorified" ‒ Hithpael, BDB 802, KB 908

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

61:2 "the favorable year of the Lord" This is an allusion to the year of
Jubilee (cf. Lev. 25:10,13,28,54). This was a year of release from all debts (i.e. an example of YHWH's mercy; note
King Zedekiah's decree in Jer. 34:8-10) and a return of all lands to the original owners every fifty years (i.e. an example
of YHWH dividing the land in Joshua. The land belonged to YHWH). There is not one example in the OT that this was
ever historically enacted. See Roland deVaux, Ancient Israel, pp. 175-177.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FEASTS OF ISRAEL, II. C.

▣ "the day of vengeance of our God" It is significant to notice that the favorable year and the
day of vengeance occur at the same time (cf. Isa. 63:4). For those who know God in the Messiah, it is a day of reward. To
those who do not know our Christ, it is a day of judgment and great sorrow (cf. Matt. 25:36-46; Rev. 20:11-15).
There must be bad news of human rebellion before there is good news of God's mercy in Christ! (cf. Romans 1-3).

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUDGMENT IN THE NT

SPECIAL TOPIC: ETERNAL PUNISHMENT

61:3 Notice the contrasts (i.e. "instead").

- a garland instead of ashes

- oil of gladness instead of mourning

- the mantle of praise instead of a spirit of fainting

Also notice the same contrast in Isa. 61:7.

- double portion instead of shame

- shout of joy instead of humiliation

▣ "garland. . .ashes" These are examples of types of things put on the head (cf. Ezek. 24:17).

▣ "The oil of gladness" The ancients lacked the availability of makeup, therefore, to prepare
themselves for times of joy and festival, they anointed themselves with olive oil (cf. Ps. 45:7).

▣ "The mantle of praise" Here is an OT example of clothing used as imagery for an attitude
and spiritual position.

▣ "oaks of righteousness. . .The planting of the Lord" In Psalm 1 it
refers to God's initiating love, ongoing support, and provision (cf. Jer. 17:7-8). Here it refers to the Messiah
(cf. Isa. 60:21).

SPECIAL TOPIC: TREES

SPECIAL TOPIC: RIGHTEOUSNESS

▣ "that He may be glorified" YHWH is glorified when His leaders and people are treated
appropriately (i.e. Mosaic Covenant).

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 61:4-9

4Then they will rebuild the ancient ruins,

They will raise up the former devastations;

And they will repair the ruined cities,

The desolations of many generations.

5Strangers will stand and pasture your flocks,

And foreigners will be your farmers and your vinedressers.

6But you will be called the priests of the Lord;

You will be spoken of as ministers of our God.

You will eat the wealth of nations,

And in their riches you will boast.

7Instead of your shame you will have a double portion,

And instead of humiliation they will shout for joy over

their portion.

Therefore they will possess a double portion in their land,

Everlasting joy will be theirs.

8For I, the Lord , love justice,

I hate robbery in the burnt offering;

And I will faithfully give them their recompense

And make an everlasting covenant with them.

9Then their offspring will be known among the nations,

And their descendants in the midst of the peoples.

All who see them will recognize them

Because they are the offspring whom the Lord has blessed.

61:4 "they will rebuild the ancient ruins" It is hard for a non-Jew to imagine the intensity of the
feeling that is connected with the Promised Land and Jersualem (cf. Isa. 49:8; 58:12; 60:10).

This verse lists several things the ones set free will do.

- rebuild the ancient ruins

- raise up the former devastations

- repair the ruined cities

The last line of Isa. 61:4 shows that the author is addressing those returning from Mesopotamian exile.
As in all of Isaiah's ambiguous poems, the historical setting is not given. The revelatory truths can apply to multiple historical situations.

61:5 Verse 5 continues the theme of foreigners coming to Jerusalem with gifts and service, to worship the God of Israel.

From NT revelation we now know that this refers to the new covenant (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36)
in Christ available for all through repentance and faith (cf. Mark 1:15; Acts 3:16,19; 20:21)!

I interpret the OT promises to national Israel as multiple fulfillment prophecies. They were
never fulfilled in Israel's history because of their sin and rebellion. They only find fulfilment in Christ.

See note at Contextual Insights, B.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WHY ARE END-TIME EVENTS SO CONTROVERSIAL?

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

61:6 "you will be called the priests of the Lord" Israel was meant to
be a nation of priests, now they will be! Peter uses this very same phrase to describe the church in 1 Pet. 2:5,9
(cf. Exod. 19:56-6; also see John's usage in Rev. 1:6).

▣

See KB 67 compared with 416.

61:7 "double portion" This refers to the inheritance of the eldest son in the
inheritance structure of ancient Israel (cf. Deut 21:17). As Israel had a double portion of YHWH's wrath
(cf. Isa. 40:2), now a double reward.

SPECIAL TOPIC: BELIEVERS' INHERITANCE

▣ "Everlasting joy will be theirs" This same wonderful promise is also found in Ps. 16:11. The
question is when will this happen.

- it did not happen to the returnees from Mesopotanian exile

- it did not happen to the Jews under Greece or Rome

- the future then

- Israel after the Messiah comes

- the church (spiritually)

- the millennium (physically)

- restored Garden of Eden (i.e. Rev. 21-22)

This is ancient, inspired poetry! It does not address all the modern questions. It is best to
take the central meaning of the strophe and view it through NT revelation (i.e. Jesus is the ultimate
revelation of the unseen God; see Contextual Insights, B)!

61:8 "For I, the Lord, love justice" YHWH is an ethical, moral being.
He demands ethical, moral actions from His people!

Note His listed characteristics.

- loves justice

- hates robbery in sacrifices (i.e. burnt offerings)

Other wonderful texts that describe YHWH's character are Exod. 34:6; Num. 14:18; Neh. 9:17;
Ps. 86:15; 103:8-14; 145:8-9!

SPECIAL TOPIC: CHARACTERISTICS OF ISRAEL'S GOD (OT)

SPECIAL TOPIC: JUSTICE

▣ "in burnt offerings" The Septuagint and possibly some variations of the Masoretic Text
have "with iniquity" (same consonants, NRSV, Peshitta, NEB, REB). The UBS Text Project, p. 156, gives the sacrificial
phrase a B rating (some doubt).

SPECIAL TOPIC: BURNT OFFERINGS

▣ "I will. . .make an everlasting covenant with them" The children of Abraham continually broke the first covenant,
as a reading of I and 2 Kings and I and 2 Chr. will show. Because of this (i.e. Lev. 26; Deut. 28), God finally allowed the
Covenant to be terminated (He left the temple, cf. Ezek. 1; 8-10). The purpose of this termination was the beginning
of a new covenant with even greater spiritual significance (cf. Jer. 31:31-34; Ezek. 36:22-36). This new covenant begins with the
birth of Jesus.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOREVER ('olam and aiōnios)

SPECIAL TOPIC: COVENANT

61:9 Here is another forever promise to Israel as a sign and message (i.e. a light, cf. Isa. 42:6; 49:6; 51:4; Acts 13:47)
about the nature of YHWH and other nations.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: ISAIAH 61:10-11

10I will rejoice greatly in the Lord,

My soul will exult in my God;

For He has clothed me with garments of salvation,

He has wrapped me with a robe of righteousness,

As a bridegroom decks himself with a garland,

And as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.

11For as the earth brings forth its sprouts,

And as a garden causes the things sown in it to spring up,

So the Lord God will cause righteousness and praise

To spring up before all the nations.

61:10 "I will rejoice greatly in the Lord,

My soul will exult in my God" This verse could refer to the Messiah or the
nation (cf. Isa. 12:1-2; 25:9; 41:16) rejoicing in YHWH's provision. The AB suggests that this chapter
has three speakers.

- the prophet, Isa. 61:1-7 (possibly the Servant)

- YHWH, Isa. 61:8-9

- personified Zion, Isa. 61:10-11 (p. 181)

This shows the ambiguity of these poems as to speakers and recipients (i.e. period of time). Many
commentators think Isa. 61:1-3 is a fifth Servant Song.

I think Isa. 61:10-11 are the restored and redeemed humanity (cf. Gen. 3:15), which is
described in Eph. 2:11-3:13; Romans 9-11.

The VERBAL PHRASE, "I will rejoice greatly," is a Qal
INFINITIVE ABSOLUTE and a Qal IMPERFECT VERB of the same root
(BDB 965, KB 1314). It was a Hebraic grammatical way of showing intensity.

The next line is parallel and the VERB "exalt" is a Qal JUSSIVE (BDB 162, KB 189).

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

SPECIAL TOPIC: MESSIANIC ERA

▣ "He has clothed me with garments of salvation" Here is an example of the joy of a wedding
feast used as imagery for the spiritual joy of knowing YHWH. This imagery is extended in the NT to refer
to believers as having Christ's robes of righteousness (cf. 2 Cor. 5:21).

Notice all the different ways of referring to festival clothing.

- clothed me with garments of salvation ‒ BDB 527, KB 519, Hiphil PERFECT

- wrapped me with a robe of righteousness ‒ BDB 418, KB 420, Qal PERFECT

- as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland ‒ BDB 464, KB 461, Piel IMPERFECT. This is
the Hebrew root, cahan, which usually refers to priests putting on their priestly garments. It is occasions such as this
that we must remember context, not lexicons, determines word meaning.

- as a bride adorns herself ‒ BDb 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT with waw

61:11 See Isa. 40:8 and 55:10-11.

DISCUSSION QUESTIONS

This is a study guide commentary, which means that you are
responsible for your own interpretation of the Bible. Each of us must walk in the light we have. You,
the Bible, and the Holy Spirit are priority in interpretation. You must not relinquish this to a commentator.

These discussion questions are provided to help you think through the major issues of this
section of the book. They are meant to be thought-provoking, not definitive.

- If this refers to the Messiah, why is it phrased in such nationalistic terms?

- Define the term Messiah.

- In what sense and to what purpose are the Jews a kingdom of priests?

- Why did God break His first everlasting covenant with the Jewish nation?

- Why is the use of a clothing metaphor in Isa. 61:10 so significant? How is it used in the NT for the believer standing before God?
